opening.text: Think of coming home after a long day. The light is on. Someone is there. The door opens, and you feel your shoulders drop. The temple is that kind of home. It is the house of the Lord. When we go there, we are welcome.

mainMessage.text: The temple is the Lord's house, and we are invited in. It is a place of peace, power and belonging.

blocks.text: **His house, not ours** The prophet Isaiah saw a day when people would go up to the house of the Lord to learn His ways.

And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Temples are houses of the Lord.
He invites us to His house.
**His peace is there** The Lord said His glory and presence would be in the house built for Him.

And inasmuch as my people build a house unto me in the name of the Lord, and do not suffer any unclean thing to come into it, that it be not defiled, my glory shall rest upon it; Yea, and my presence shall be there, for I will come into it, and all the pure in heart that shall come into it shall see God.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Right Before Our Eyes” from the April 2025 general conference.
In His house we can feel the Lord’s hallowed presence and transcendent peace.
Peace lives at the Lord's house.
**A shelter from the storm** When life gets loud, a good house is a refuge. Isaiah called the Lord a refuge from the storm.

For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
I promise you that over time, the temple will become a place of safety, solace, and revelation.
Give it time, and it becomes home.
**Power for the road** When the Kirtland Temple was dedicated, the Saints asked that the people would leave armed with God's power.

And we ask thee, Holy Father, that thy servants may go forth from this house armed with thy power, and that thy name may be upon them, and thy glory be round about them, and thine angels have charge over them;
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Frequent participation in the ordinances of the temple can create a pattern of devotion to the Lord.
Go often, and the pattern becomes devotion.
**Family joined together** In the temple, the hearts of families are turned toward each other, across generations.

Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Atonement of Jesus Christ Provides the Ultimate Rescue” from the April 2025 general conference.
Temple attendance allows us to provide a spiritual rescue for our deceased loved ones and more distant ancestors.
Love can reach across the years.
**Get the house ready** The Lord asked His people to prepare and to establish a house for Him.

Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
If you don’t yet love to attend the temple, go more often—not less.
Love for the temple grows with going.

story.title: The glory fills the house

blocks.text: King Solomon had built a temple. When it was finished, something happened that no one could miss.

And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the Lord, So that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of the Lord had filled the house of the Lord.
The Lord showed that He accepted the house. His glory was there. He still blesses His houses today.

application.text: First, think of a time you felt peace in a holy place. Second, plan a visit to a temple, or to the temple grounds if you can't go in. Third, bring one question and listen.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the temple is the house of the Lord. I know He welcomes us there. I know peace is found in His house. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

blessings: You will feel peace in the house of the Lord.
You will be taught by the Spirit.

closingVerse.text: And that all people who shall enter upon the threshold of the Lord’s house may feel thy power, and feel constrained to acknowledge that thou hast sanctified it, and that it is thy house, a place of thy holiness.

opening.text: After a bad storm, a boat finds a harbor. The water is calm there. Ropes are tied. Someone has a light on. The boat is safe. For many people, the temple is a harbor. They come in from the storm and find rest.

mainMessage.text: The temple is a harbor for our souls. It is a place to rest, to be strengthened and to set out again.

blocks.text: **The harbor was built by the Lord** The house is His. He invites all people to come to it.

And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Temples are houses of the Lord.
The harbor is open.
**Still water** Outside, the sea is rough. Inside the harbor, the water is still. The Lord promised His presence in His house.

And inasmuch as my people build a house unto me in the name of the Lord, and do not suffer any unclean thing to come into it, that it be not defiled, my glory shall rest upon it; Yea, and my presence shall be there, for I will come into it, and all the pure in heart that shall come into it shall see God.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Right Before Our Eyes” from the April 2025 general conference.
In His house we can feel the Lord’s hallowed presence and transcendent peace.
Quiet water is a gift.
**Shelter from the wind** A harbor breaks the force of the storm. The Lord is called a refuge from the storm.

For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
I promise you that over time, the temple will become a place of safety, solace, and revelation.
You are safe here.
**Refueled to sail again** Boats don't stay in the harbor. They rest, then they go out. We leave the temple with strength.

And we ask thee, Holy Father, that thy servants may go forth from this house armed with thy power, and that thy name may be upon them, and thy glory be round about them, and thine angels have charge over them;
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Frequent participation in the ordinances of the temple can create a pattern of devotion to the Lord.
Rest, then sail out again.
**Ships come home together** A harbor holds many boats. In the temple, families are joined, and those who are gone are not forgotten.

Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Atonement of Jesus Christ Provides the Ultimate Rescue” from the April 2025 general conference.
Temple attendance allows us to provide a spiritual rescue for our deceased loved ones and more distant ancestors.
We bring our family into the harbor.
**Keep the harbor ready** A good harbor is maintained. The Lord asked His people to prepare and establish a house.

Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
If you don’t yet love to attend the temple, go more often—not less.
Come back to the harbor often.

story.title: Jesus in the temple at twelve

blocks.text: When Jesus was a boy, His family went to Jerusalem. After three days they found Him in the temple.

And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions. And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers.
Even as a boy, He felt at home in His Father's house. We can learn to feel at home there too.

application.text: First, name a storm you are facing. Second, set aside a time to go to the temple or to pray about it. Third, write down what you feel.

blocks.text: I know the temple is a place of rest. I know the Lord gives strength to those who come. I know Jesus Christ opens the door. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

closingVerse.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;

opening.text: When you climb to a high place, the view changes. Things that looked big below look small. Your worries shrink. You can see the road you took. The temple is a high place like that. We go up to it, and we see our lives more clearly.

mainMessage.text: The temple lifts our view. In the Lord's house, we see our lives the way He does.

blocks.text: **The mountain of the Lord** Isaiah called the temple the mountain of the Lord's house. It is a high place that people go up to.

And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Temples are houses of the Lord.
The climb is worth it.
**Thin air, clear peace** Up high, the air is clear and quiet. In the temple, the Lord's presence brings that kind of quiet.

And inasmuch as my people build a house unto me in the name of the Lord, and do not suffer any unclean thing to come into it, that it be not defiled, my glory shall rest upon it; Yea, and my presence shall be there, for I will come into it, and all the pure in heart that shall come into it shall see God.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Right Before Our Eyes” from the April 2025 general conference.
In His house we can feel the Lord’s hallowed presence and transcendent peace.
The air is calm up here.
**Above the storm** Sometimes clouds sit below the summit. The storm is still there. But up here, we are above it.

For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
I promise you that over time, the temple will become a place of safety, solace, and revelation.
From here, the storm looks smaller.
**Going back down with strength** We don't live on the summit. We go back down. But we carry what we gained.

And we ask thee, Holy Father, that thy servants may go forth from this house armed with thy power, and that thy name may be upon them, and thy glory be round about them, and thine angels have charge over them;
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Frequent participation in the ordinances of the temple can create a pattern of devotion to the Lord.
Climb often, and the strength stays.
**A view of all the generations** From a high place, we can see far. In the temple, we see back to our ancestors and forward to our children.

Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Atonement of Jesus Christ Provides the Ultimate Rescue” from the April 2025 general conference.
Temple attendance allows us to provide a spiritual rescue for our deceased loved ones and more distant ancestors.
We see our whole family from here.
**Prepare for the climb** A climb takes preparing. The Lord asked His people to prepare every needful thing and establish a house for Him.

Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
If you don’t yet love to attend the temple, go more often—not less.
Start climbing, and love grows.

story.title: The Lord accepts the Kirtland Temple

blocks.text: After the Saints built the Kirtland Temple with great sacrifice, the Lord spoke.

For behold, I have accepted this house, and my name shall be here; and I will manifest myself to my people in mercy in this house. Yea, I will appear unto my servants, and speak unto them with mine own voice, if my people will keep my commandments, and do not pollute this holy house.
The Saints gave much to build it. The Lord promised His mercy there. He does the same in His houses today.

application.text: First, think of a problem that feels big. Second, bring it to the Lord in a quiet place. Third, write down any new thoughts that come.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the temple is a high place. I know that the Lord shows us the bigger picture there. I know Jesus Christ is the reason we go. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think of a problem that feels big.

closingVerse.text: But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

opening.text: Your phone gets low on battery. You plug it in, and an hour later, it's ready. Nothing about the phone changed. It just got power. The temple is a place we plug into God's power. We come in tired, and we leave with strength.

mainMessage.text: The temple is where God charges His people with strength. We come in low and leave filled.

blocks.text: **The charging station is His** The power comes from the Lord, and He built the house for it.

And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Temples are houses of the Lord.
Go to the source.
**Quiet while it charges** A phone has to sit still to charge. We sit still in the temple. The Lord's peace fills us.

And inasmuch as my people build a house unto me in the name of the Lord, and do not suffer any unclean thing to come into it, that it be not defiled, my glory shall rest upon it; Yea, and my presence shall be there, for I will come into it, and all the pure in heart that shall come into it shall see God.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Right Before Our Eyes” from the April 2025 general conference.
In His house we can feel the Lord’s hallowed presence and transcendent peace.
Stillness lets the power in.
**A safe place to plug in** You plug in where it is safe. The temple becomes a refuge where we can rest and receive.

For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
I promise you that over time, the temple will become a place of safety, solace, and revelation.
This is a safe place to be filled.
**Fully charged** The Saints at Kirtland prayed that the people would go forth armed with God's power. That is the purpose.

And we ask thee, Holy Father, that thy servants may go forth from this house armed with thy power, and that thy name may be upon them, and thy glory be round about them, and thine angels have charge over them;
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Frequent participation in the ordinances of the temple can create a pattern of devotion to the Lord.
A habit keeps the charge up.
**Power to help others** The power isn't just for us. In the temple, we can serve those who have passed on.

Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Atonement of Jesus Christ Provides the Ultimate Rescue” from the April 2025 general conference.
Temple attendance allows us to provide a spiritual rescue for our deceased loved ones and more distant ancestors.
Strength shared is strength doubled.
**Don't wait for empty** We don't wait for zero battery to charge. President Nelson says to go more often, even if it doesn't feel natural yet.

Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
If you don’t yet love to attend the temple, go more often—not less.
Charge before you need to.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they left the temple feeling stronger than when they came. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Isaiah is cleansed and sent

blocks.text: Isaiah saw a vision of the Lord's house. An angel touched his lips and took away his sin.

Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar: And he laid it upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged. Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.
Isaiah came in feeling unworthy. He left saying, "Send me." That is what a temple can do.

closingVerse.text: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

opening.text: In dry country, people remember where the wells are. They plan their trips around them. A well means water, and water means life. For our spirits, the temple is a well. It is a place where living water is found. We can come back to it again and again.

mainMessage.text: The temple is a well for the soul. Anyone who is thirsty can come and drink.

blocks.text: **A well in the high country** The prophets said people from all nations would come to the Lord's house, like travelers coming to water.

And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Temples are houses of the Lord.
The well is there for all of us.
**Cool and quiet** The water at a well is cool. The Lord says His glory and presence rest in His house.

And inasmuch as my people build a house unto me in the name of the Lord, and do not suffer any unclean thing to come into it, that it be not defiled, my glory shall rest upon it; Yea, and my presence shall be there, for I will come into it, and all the pure in heart that shall come into it shall see God.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Right Before Our Eyes” from the April 2025 general conference.
In His house we can feel the Lord’s hallowed presence and transcendent peace.
Refreshment is found in His house.
**A shadow in the heat** A well often has shade beside it. Isaiah says the Lord is a shadow from the heat.

For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
I promise you that over time, the temple will become a place of safety, solace, and revelation.
He offers shade for tired travelers.
**Filling the jar** A traveler fills a jar and carries it onward. We leave the temple carrying strength for the road.

And we ask thee, Holy Father, that thy servants may go forth from this house armed with thy power, and that thy name may be upon them, and thy glory be round about them, and thine angels have charge over them;
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants” from the April 2024 general conference.
Frequent participation in the ordinances of the temple can create a pattern of devotion to the Lord.
A steady habit keeps the jar full.
**Water for those who can't come** Some people can't come to the well themselves. We can carry water for them, by serving in the temple for our ancestors.

Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Atonement of Jesus Christ Provides the Ultimate Rescue” from the April 2025 general conference.
Temple attendance allows us to provide a spiritual rescue for our deceased loved ones and more distant ancestors.
We can carry water for our family.
**Keep the path to the well clear** A path stays open when people use it. The Lord asked His people to prepare and establish His house.

Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God;
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Temple and Your Spiritual Foundation” from the October 2021 general conference.
If you don’t yet love to attend the temple, go more often—not less.
The path stays open when we use it.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they or their family worked hard to be near a temple. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nephi builds a temple

blocks.text: Nephi and his people were far from Jerusalem. They had little. But they built a temple.

And I, Nephi, did build a temple; and I did construct it after the manner of the temple of Solomon save it were not built of so many precious things; for they were not to be found upon the land, wherefore, it could not be built like unto Solomon’s temple. But the manner of the construction was like unto the temple of Solomon; and the workmanship thereof was exceedingly fine.
They did not have many precious things. They still built the Lord a house. Their well was dug with what they had.

application.text: First, ask yourself what you need to drink in right now. Second, set a time to go to the temple, or to prepare for it. Third, share what you learn with someone you love.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the temple is a well of living water. I know the Lord invites every person to come. I know Jesus Christ is the living water. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to ask yourself what you need to drink in right now.
I invite you to set a time to go to the temple, or to prepare for it.
I invite you to share what you learn with someone you love.
blessings: You will feel the Savior's love.
Someone you love will be strengthened.

closingVerse.text: And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
